name: Trustless Work
description:
Trustless Work is a verified Stellar Wave Program DeFi infrastructure project focused on non-custodial smart-contract escrow on Stellar. Its Wave-approved repository, official website, and developer documentation all describe the product as escrow-as-a-service built on Stellar and Soroban for stablecoin-based transactions. In practical terms, Trustless Work provides a financial primitive that sits inside the DeFi stack: programmable escrow. Instead of relying on a centralized platform or marketplace operator to custody funds and manually release them, the protocol deploys Soroban escrow contracts that hold funds on-chain until role-based conditions are met.

The core on-chain mechanic is milestone-based escrow. A user or integrating platform creates an escrow contract, defines the relevant roles, selects the asset, and specifies whether the deal is single-release or multi-release. Funds are then deposited into the Soroban contract and remain non-custodial until milestones are approved, a release signer authorizes payout, or a dispute resolver intervenes. Trustless Work's public docs explain the full escrow lifecycle, including deployment, funding, milestone updates, approvals, releases, and disputes. The API and SDK expose these actions so marketplaces, crowdfunding apps, and P2P exchanges can integrate trust-minimized settlement without writing their own contracts from scratch.

From a DeFi perspective, Trustless Work is not a DEX or lending pool; it is settlement-layer DeFi infrastructure for conditional payments. It enables capital to be locked, programmatically governed, and released according to transparent smart-contract logic on Stellar. The docs explicitly position the protocol for use cases such as freelance contracts, crowdfunding, pre-orders, security deposits, marketplaces, and OTC or P2P exchange flows. Public docs and repo material also confirm the protocol uses Stellar-native rails and supports assets such as USDC, making it relevant to the broader DeFi and stablecoin ecosystem on Stellar.
asset_focus: Programmable non-custodial escrow for stablecoin-based transactions on Stellar
issuance_model: Trustless Work does not issue a standalone token in the reviewed public sources. Instead, it deploys Soroban escrow contracts that hold Stellar-native assets such as USDC and release them according to milestone, approval, and dispute rules.
compliance_model: The protocol is non-custodial and positions itself as infrastructure. Compliance obligations depend on the integrating platform, asset used, and jurisdiction. Public docs emphasize programmable escrow and stablecoin settlement rather than a regulated issuance model.
audit_status: A public third-party audit report was not identified in the reviewed sources. Public documentation and repository materials do show detailed deployment, lifecycle, API, and contract-operations guidance.
supported_markets: Freelance and contract work, milestone-based services, marketplaces, crowdfunding, pre-orders, security deposits, P2P exchanges, and OTC-style stablecoin settlement flows.
trading_pairs: Not a trading protocol. Trustless Work is a DeFi settlement primitive rather than an exchange market.
on_chain_volume: On-chain activity is escrow-specific rather than aggregated in the public docs reviewed. Each escrow is deployed as a Soroban contract and can be verified via transaction hash, escrow contract ID, Stellar explorer queries, and the Trustless Work viewer/API flows described in the documentation.
stellar_contract_id: Deployment-specific escrow contract IDs are generated per escrow instance and referenced in the public docs as the escrow ID / contract ID. The reviewed public sources do not expose one canonical live production ID.
tags: defi, escrow, soroban, stablecoins, usdc, milestone-payments, smart-contracts, settlement
